output.brief: Don't discipline drivers or retrain everyone. The evidence points to contaminated brake fluid. Northfield Motor Services changed the fluid in 13 Eastgate vans during the bay closure, mostly from an old bulk drum with a missing cap, and the drum had absorbed water. Two vans retested there on 24 Sep had fluid boiling at about 150°C, against 255°C for sealed stock. The 11 vans with complaints are all among the 13 Northfield vans. The two Northfield vans that got fluid from a fresh drum had no complaints. Pad batches were split about evenly between garages, and every van ran Upper Wend about as often. The same drivers reported no problems in other vans, so technique and hill routes don't explain it. Northfield's 25 Sep recommendation to recheck the other vans got no reply. I'm fairly confident, around 85–90%. Next: pull every Northfield-serviced van from service this week, boiling-point test it, renew the fluid from sealed stock, and then return it to the pool. Keep LK-209 parked until that is done. Tell drivers that reporting is safe. Consider checking the Calder Road vans and pad noise separately.
